name: Knowledge: source classification
description: Minimal workflow for classifying candidate knowledge sources before extraction. Classification policy is carried as workflow documents attached to executable functions.

documents.name: Knowledge source classification policy
documents.content: Classify each source before extraction. Return source_type, intake_decision, sensitivity, confidence, summary_required, escalation_reason, and extraction_scope. source_type must be one of: meeting_transcript, chat_thread, proposal, adr, external_article, unknown. intake_decision must be one of: ingest, summarize_only, ignore, escalate. Meeting transcript: ingest when it contains durable decisions, owners, deadlines, requirements, or risks; summarize_only when it is status chatter; escalate when consent, customer confidentiality, or unclear ownership is present. Chat thread: ingest decisions, incidents, agreements, and reusable context; ignore greetings, duplicate notifications, transient coordination, and pure bot noise; escalate private data or unresolved conflict. Proposal: ingest approved scope, assumptions, terms, risks, and client commitments; summarize_only drafts; escalate pricing or legal ambiguity. ADR: ingest accepted or superseded decisions with context, alternatives, consequences, and owner; escalate contradictory or missing status. External article: summarize_only unless explicitly curated for the KB; ignore thin marketing pages and duplicates; escalate licensing, paywall, or trust concerns. Never invent missing facts.

documents.name: Knowledge source classification output schema
documents.content: Output JSON fields: source_type:string, intake_decision:string, sensitivity:string, confidence:number, summary_required:boolean, extraction_scope:string[], evidence:string[], escalation_reason:string|null, ignored_reason:string|null. evidence must cite source-local facts. extraction_scope should name the durable parts to extract, such as decisions, assumptions, owners, deadlines, risks, API contracts, product requirements, or operational runbook steps.
